explanation: Microwaves reach only a few centimetres into food, so the centre warms by conduction from the outside. That is why recipes say to stir dishes and let them stand.

claims.text: Microwave ovens heat food mainly by making water molecules rotate back and forth.
Microwave ovens do not heat food mainly through salt, sugar or protein molecules.
Microwaves penetrate only a few centimetres into food, and deeper parts heat by conduction.
Stirring and standing time let heat spread through microwaved food.
